text: I have a 40-hectare suckler beef farm in West Cork. About 3 hectares beside the river are too wet for the cattle. What grants could I get for that land?

missing: whether you are an active farmer

summary: You are likely to get the Native Tree Area Scheme, where you could get up to €58,388 over 10 years, including a one-off grant of €6,744 per ha and yearly premiums, though a registered forester must check your soil and site. You are also likely to qualify for the Basic Income Support for Sustainability by claiming on your eligible hectares, with entitlement values up to €285. You should check the Areas of Natural Constraint for payments between €93 and €148 per ha by confirming your townland. Finally, check if you can join the Agri-Climate Rural Environment Scheme, which pays up to €7,311 or €10,500 a year.

text: I'm 29 and I took over the home farm last year: 60 hectares of dairy in Tipperary. I'd like to put solar panels on the milking parlour roof.

missing: whether you are near a watercourse

summary: You are likely to get the Basic Income Support for Sustainability, which pays on your eligible hectares using entitlements that in 2026 are worth no more than €285, and you claim this annually alongside other schemes. You should also check the Areas of Natural Constraint scheme, which pays from €93 to €148 per hectare if your land is in a designated area and you meet stocking rules. You need to check if you can join the Agri-Climate Rural Environment Scheme for payments up to €7,311 or €10,500 depending on the strand, and finally check the Solar Capital Investment Scheme for your solar plans since rules are not yet verified.

text: I farm 35 hectares of sheep in Kerry with my husband, and I am planning to build a new slatted shed next year.
summary: You are likely to get the Basic Income Support for Sustainability, which pays on your eligible hectares up to your payment entitlements, with none above €285 in 2026, and you should claim this yearly. You need to check the Areas of Natural Constraint, which pays from €93 to €148 per hectare on your first hectares if your land is designated. You must also check the Agri-Climate Rural Environment Scheme, which pays up to €7,311 a year for ACRES General or up to €10,500 in priority areas. Finally, check the Animal Welfare and Nutrient Storage Scheme, where rules and rates are not yet verified.
